title: Electron Beam-Induced Phase Transformations in Different Crystal Orientations of a 2D van der Waals Magnet
content: Understanding and controlling material properties at the atomic scale is not only essential for unraveling fundamental physics, but also for paving the way towards novel devices that exploit size- and structure-dependent electronic and optical phenomena [1, 2]. The recently-discovered family of layered two-dimensional (2D) magnetic materials provide an ideal platform to assess such controllability. These materials, with their well-defined vertical dimensions and surfaces, present exciting opportunities for seamless integration with conventional device materials [3, 4]. To control materials properties at the nanoscale, the well-focused electron beam of the scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) can be used as a tool to engineer structure with atomic precision [5]. For 2D magnets, especially the highly anisotropic materials AgCrP2S6 and CrSBr, we find that the STEM serves as a powerful tool for sculpting the arrangement of atoms, with the potential to modulate local magnetic properties [5, 6].
